messages.subject: Test if detection probabilities are equal
messages.subject_clean: Test if detection probabilities are equal
messages.body_plain:
Hello,
I am doing some analyses using camera trap data but there are a few
species that have very small detection probabilities (<0.04) so the
occupancy estimates I get are biased. One possibility is to group all
these species together and test whether their detection probabilities
are equal and if they are, fix the detection probability in the model
to estimate only the occupancy. How do it test this (DP are =) using
unmarked?

Thanks,

Jorge

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Test if detection probabilities are equal
messages.subject_clean: [unmarked] Test if detection probabilities are equal
messages.body_plain:
hi Jorge,
 you can fit the full model (i.e., with species-specific p) and then the reduced model and then do a standard likelihood ratio statistic.

D = -2*[log(lik full model) - log(lik reduced model)]

which has, approximately, a chi-square distribution with df = difference in the df between the full and reduced models.  Thus, considering H0: p1=p2=....pK  vs Ha: not all p's equal
you would reject  if you have a large value of D (look it up in a chi-square table)

regards
andy

messages.subject: Re: Predict using a colext object
messages.body_plain:
Hi Giancarlo,

The two relevant help pages are:

help("unmarkedFit-class")
help(linearComb)

They could use some work, but in there you will see that there is a
_names_ method that returns the names of the parameter types. So:

> names(fm.yearly)
[1] "psi" "col" "ext" "det"

After you decide which type of prediction you want, you need to give
linearComb specific covariate values (2nd argument).

lc <- linearComb(fm.yearly, c(1,0,1,0,0,0), type="ext") # is equivalent to:
lc <- linearComb(fm.yearly, coefficients=c(Int=1, year2=0, year3=1,
year4=0, year5=0, year6=0), type="ext")

Note that coefficients can be a properly formatted design matrix too.
The only advantage of the _predict_ method is that it creates the
design matrix for you. Hopefully this will be part of the next
release...sometime in the Fall maybe.

Richard

Quoting Giancarlo Sadoti <gcsa...@gmail.com>:

> Hi Richard and Ian,
>
> Your reply to Ben helps me understand things, but can you enlighten me
> a bit further on the syntax for using linearcomb()?
>
> e.g, lc <- linearComb(fm.yearly, c(1,0,1,0,0,0), type="col")
>
> I've used predict() to get occupancy probabilities from occu models
> (thanks for including this).
>
> I have a two season design and would like to estimate probabilities of
> both colonization and extirpation.  (e.g., is type='removal' for
> extirpation?)
>
> Thanks for all you've done with this package.  It has saved me time
> beyond measure!
>
> Giancarlo

>
>
> On May 13, 12:21 pm, rchand...@nrc.umass.edu wrote:
>> I will put that on the to-do list. In the meantime, note that predict
>> is basically just a convenience wrapper for linearComb. See
>> ?linearComb for examples of getting predictions without predict. And
>> continuing with the colext example, you can do something like this:
>>
>> # Logit-scale estimate of colonization prob in year 3
>> lc <- linearComb(fm.yearly, c(1,0,1,0,0,0), type="col")
>>
>> # Back-transform it and get confidence interval
>>
>> confint(backTransform(lc))
>>
>> Richard
>

--
